# CLEARS - Model Evaluation Report (v2)
**Owner:** Person 2 - ML & Explainability Lead | **Generated by:** `src/make_model_report.py` from `data/models/metrics.json`
**Data:** `features_final_v2.csv` (see `data_quality_report_v2.md`) | **Library versions:** XGBoost 3.2.0, scikit-learn 1.8.0, pandas 2.2.3

> **Headline.** On a time-ordered, out-of-sample test set the disruption model reaches **F1 = 0.343** for the disruption class
> (precision 0.327, recall 0.361) and **ROC-AUC = 0.650**. The project target of F1 >= 0.70 is
> **NOT met**. A date-grouped cross-validation, which is easier than a time-ordered test, reaches only
> F1 = 0.393 and ROC-AUC = 0.708, so the gap to 0.70 is not caused by the
> split. Weather timing in the data is also known to be wrong (see Limitations), so these results are provisional until the data is regenerated.

## 1. Model architecture
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Disruption model | `XGBClassifier`, binary, `scale_pos_weight` = 4.80 (negatives / positives in training), histogram trees |
| Selected hyper-parameters | max_depth 7, learning_rate 0.05, 15 trees (early stopping, 30 rounds, validation PR-AUC), subsample 0.8, colsample 0.8, min_child_weight 5 |
| Search | guide grid (depth 3/5/7 x learning rate 0.05/0.1), n_estimators by early stopping; chosen on the **validation** slice by PR-AUC. All six configurations scored within 0.002 PR-AUC of each other |
| Probability calibration | isotonic regression fitted on the validation slice, so `probability` is a real probability (the raw `scale_pos_weight` output is inflated: Brier 0.2344 raw vs 0.1411 calibrated vs 0.1502 for a constant) |
| Decision threshold | 0.213 on the calibrated probability, the F1-optimal value on the validation slice |
| Inputs (20) | `wind_speed_knots`, `visibility_km`, `temperature_c`, `humidity_pct`, `precip_mm_hr`, `wind_category_enc`, `visibility_risk`, `rain_severity_enc`, `temp_stress`, `storm_flag`, `hour_of_day`, `day_of_week`, `month`, `is_peak_hour`, `is_weekend`, `delay_last_1h`, `delay_last_3h`, `delay_last_24h`, `congestion_level`, `runway_count` |
| Excluded | every label-derived column (`dep_delay`, `arr_delay`, `delay_minutes`, `cancelled`, `*_delay`), identifiers and constants - see `feature_dictionary_v2.md` Section 9 |
| Severity model | `XGBClassifier(objective='multi:softprob', num_class=4)`, balanced sample weights, depth 3, learning rate 0.1, 53 trees |
| Scenario (what-if) model | XGBoost on weather + time + airport only (no delay history), monotone constraints, depth 4, learning rate 0.03, 562 trees, isotonic-calibrated |
| Saved files | `data/models/disruption_model.pkl`, `severity_model.pkl`, `scenario_model.pkl` (dicts holding the model, calibrator, threshold, feature list and training medians; load with the same library versions) |

## 2. Training data
| Slice | Dates | Rows | Disruption rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Train | 2019-01-01 to 2021-07-31 | 248,613 | 17.2% |
| Validation (early stopping, calibration, threshold) | 2021-10-01 to 2022-01-31 | 48,508 | 20.2% |
| **Test (used once)** | 2022-04-01 to 2022-10-31 | 73,608 | 18.4% |

Airports ORD and MEM, only January/April/July/October of each year (492 days). Split on whole dates, strictly time-ordered; the test set
contains **no winter month** (April, July and October 2022 only). Class ratio about 4.8 : 1.

## 3. Test metrics - disruption model (threshold 0.213, chosen on validation)
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | 0.746 |
| Precision / recall / **F1** (disruption class) | 0.327 / 0.361 / **0.343** |
| Precision / recall / F1 (no-disruption class) | 0.853 / 0.833 / 0.843 |
| ROC-AUC | 0.650 |
| PR-AUC (a random model scores 0.184) | 0.322 |

Full `classification_report` output for both models: `data/models/classification_report.txt`.

Confusion matrix (test, rows = truth):

| | predicted no disruption | predicted disruption |
|---|---|---|
| **actual no disruption** | 50,033 | 10,042 |
| **actual disruption** | 8,649 | 4,884 |

At the uncalibrated 0.5 cut-off the same model gives precision 0.266, recall 0.559, F1 0.360
(TP 7,569, FP 20,891, FN 5,964, TN 39,184); the validation-chosen threshold is not better on the test months because the
disruption regime differs (validation 20.2% vs test 18.4%).

## 4. Comparison with baselines
| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 (disruption) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flag every flight | 0.500 | 0.184 | 0.311 |
| Delay-history signal alone (`delay_last_3h` as a score) | 0.634 | 0.287 | - |
| Logistic regression (same 20 inputs, same protocol) | 0.644 | 0.303 | 0.323 |
| **XGBoost (this model)** | **0.650** | **0.322** | **0.343** |

XGBoost improves on logistic regression by 0.020 F1 (6.3% relative) and 0.006 ROC-AUC. That is a small
gain, not the "substantial improvement" the project report expects. The weather-only baseline in `notebooks/02_baseline_model.ipynb`
scores ROC-AUC 0.585 and F1 0.31, no better than flagging every flight.

**Which inputs matter (retrained on feature groups, same protocol)**

| Feature group | Inputs | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| full | 20 | 0.650 | 0.322 | 0.343 |
| weather only | 10 | 0.586 | 0.224 | 0.332 |
| time only | 6 | 0.605 | 0.235 | 0.340 |
| no history features | 16 | 0.618 | 0.252 | 0.335 |

Delay history is worth about +0.032 ROC-AUC on top of weather + time; weather alone is the weakest group.

**Is the low score a split artefact?** No.

| Evaluation | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time-ordered test (this report) | 0.650 | 0.322 | 0.343 |
| Train before 2022, test 2022 (whole year) | 0.658 | 0.352 | - |
| Train before 2021, test 2021 | 0.702 | 0.365 | - |
| Date-grouped 5-fold CV (optimistic, not time-ordered) | 0.708 | 0.393 | 0.393 |

## 5. Top 10 SHAP features (mean |SHAP| on the test set, log-odds of the raw model)
SHAP values are exact TreeSHAP from XGBoost (`pred_contribs`), identical to `shap.TreeExplainer`; they sum to the model output (checked in `model_verification.md`). Plot: `assets/shap_summary.png`.

| # | Feature | Mean abs SHAP | Share | What it measures | Does it make sense? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `delay_last_3h` | 0.2822 | 33.7% | Share of flights disrupted in the 3-hour window ending two hours before this flight | Delays cascade: a disrupted airport tends to stay disrupted. The strongest and most intuitive signal. |
| 2 | `delay_last_1h` | 0.1219 | 14.6% | Disruption share in the single hour ending two hours before | Same cascade effect, shorter memory. |
| 3 | `delay_last_24h` | 0.1196 | 14.3% | Disruption share over the previous 24 hours | Captures a bad day (weather system, ground stop) rather than a bad hour. |
| 4 | `hour_of_day` | 0.1052 | 12.6% | Scheduled departure hour | Delays accumulate through the day, so late hours are riskier (about 8% at 05:00, 21-25% in the evening). |
| 5 | `congestion_level` | 0.0725 | 8.7% | Scheduled departures in the two previous hours | A busier airport has less slack; plausible, and it also proxies the time of day. |
| 6 | `temperature_c` | 0.0455 | 5.4% | Air temperature | Acts mostly as a season proxy (hot July afternoons with thunderstorms and high traffic) rather than a direct cause. |
| 7 | `humidity_pct` | 0.0289 | 3.5% | Relative humidity | Also season/convective-weather proxy; not a direct operational driver. |
| 8 | `visibility_km` | 0.0143 | 1.7% | Horizontal visibility | Low visibility forces instrument procedures and spacing; sensible, but a small effect once delay history is known. |
| 9 | `wind_speed_knots` | 0.0135 | 1.6% | Wind speed | Strong wind restricts runway use; sensible, small effect (max wind in the data is 30 kn). |
| 10 | `runway_count` | 0.0123 | 1.5% | Number of runways (ORD 8, MEM 4) | Only an airport identifier here (two airports); do not read it as a capacity effect. |

**The weather flags the project report names as leading predictors contribute almost nothing:** `visibility_risk` 0.02%, `storm_flag` 0.01%,
`wind_category_enc` 0.10% of total importance; only `delay_last_3h` (33.7%) is a leading predictor. The flags are rare (storm flag 0.45% of flights) and,
once delay history is known, add little. In the raw data, though, flights with visibility < 3 km are disrupted 39.1% of the time vs 17.5% otherwise, so the effect exists; the model attributes it to the delay history that
bad weather produces.

## 6. Delay severity model
Classes: none (not disrupted), minor (15-45 min), moderate (45-120 min), severe (> 120 min). Balanced class weights.

| Class | Test flights | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 60,075 | 0.871 | 0.637 | 0.736 |
| minor | 6,812 | 0.110 | 0.235 | 0.150 |
| moderate | 4,876 | 0.116 | 0.204 | 0.148 |
| severe | 1,845 | 0.075 | 0.265 | 0.117 |

Accuracy 0.562, **macro-F1 0.288** (always predicting "none" would score accuracy 0.816 but macro-F1 about 0.2). Confusion matrix (rows = truth, columns = prediction):

| | none | minor | moderate | severe |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| true none | 38,290 | 11,542 | 6,064 | 4,179 |
| true minor | 3,133 | 1,602 | 1,169 | 908 |
| true moderate | 1,923 | 1,043 | 995 | 915 |
| true severe | 605 | 394 | 357 | 489 |

The severity classes are only weakly separable from the available inputs (F1 0.12-0.15 for the three delay classes). Use the severity output as a coarse indication and show the class probabilities, not the label alone.

## 7. Probability bands and the dashboard
With the calibrated probability, KPI 4 bands (Low < 0.3, Medium 0.3-0.65, High > 0.65) split the test flights as:

| Band | Share of flights | Observed disruption rate |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 89.9% | 15.8% |
| Medium | 9.2% | - |
| High | 0.9% | 73.0% |

The probabilities are well calibrated at the top (High-band flights are disrupted 73% of the time), but with an 18% base rate almost every flight is "Low" and the gauge will
rarely leave green. The team should choose bands with this in mind (for example by relative risk: base rate x 1.5, x 2).

## 8. Scenario simulator
The full model reacts only weakly to weather overrides (about +4 points for 0.5 km visibility + 10 mm/h rain + 28 kn wind with delay history held fixed), because bad weather reaches it mainly through the delay-history inputs.
`scenario_risk()` therefore uses by default a **weather + time model without delay history** (monotone: worse weather never lowers the risk). Its test ROC-AUC is 0.620. Mean change in probability on test flights:

| Scenario | Change in probability |
|---|---|
| low visibility (0.5 km) | +0.067 |
| heavy rain (10 mm/h) | +0.028 |
| strong wind (28 kn) | +0.089 |
| all three together | +0.236 |
| clear day (16 km, dry, 5 kn) | -0.009 |

Interpretation: "the disruption risk under these conditions before delays have accumulated". Its `base_probability` is not the gauge value (that is the full model). Wind above the training maximum (30.3 kn) is treated like 30 kn.

## 9. Resilience index methodology
Inputs per airport (from `airport_resilience_inputs_v2.csv`): disruption rate, average delay of disrupted flights ("recovery time"), weather sensitivity = correlation(`storm_flag`, `disruption`), congestion sensitivity = correlation(`congestion_level`, `disruption`).
Formula: min-max normalise each across airports; vulnerability = 0.35 x disruption rate + 0.30 x recovery time + 0.20 x weather sensitivity + 0.15 x congestion sensitivity; index = 100 - 100 x vulnerability; tiers <= 40 Vulnerable, 40-70 Moderate, > 70 Resilient.
Weights are a design choice: frequency (0.35) and severity of delays (0.30) are what operations experience most directly; the two correlation terms (0.20 / 0.15) describe sensitivity rather than outcomes and are weaker, noisier measures. The literature does not fix the weights.

| Airport | Disruption rate | Avg delay of disrupted flights (min) | Weather sens. | Congestion sens. | Resilience index | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MEM | 0.1548 | 70.6 | 0.0102 | 0.0460 | **70.0** | Moderate |
| ORD | 0.1806 | 68.2 | 0.0415 | 0.0793 | **30.0** | Vulnerable |

**Limitation that matters:** with two airports min-max scaling maps every dimension to exactly 0 or 1, so the scores (30 and 70) only say which airport is higher on each dimension, not by how much - MEM's 70.6 vs ORD's 68.2 minutes of average delay receives the full 0.30 weight. In 2022 MEM's
disruption rate (20.7%) is higher than ORD's (18.2%), the opposite of the full-period ranking. Do not present the index as more than a two-airport ranking.

## 11. Known limitations
1. **Weather is ~5-6 hours out of sync with departure times in the data** (UTC vs local; data quality report, Check 8). Weather effects, SHAP conclusions and the scenario model are provisional. Retrain with `CLEARS_DATA=<regenerated file> python src/model_train.py` once `data_prep.py` has been run on the raw data.
2. **Modest predictive power.** F1 0.343 / ROC-AUC 0.650; even the optimistic date-grouped CV only reaches F1 0.393. The inputs (weather, time, short delay history) simply do not determine disruption well; schedule/airline/route data would be needed.
3. **Small, unrepresentative coverage:** four months per year, two airports, no winter month in the test set, 2020 is an outlier year, most cancelled flights were removed (understating disruption).
4. **Regime shift:** thresholds tuned on the October-January validation slice do not transfer to October 2022 (F1 0.082 that month).
5. **No real-time feed:** inputs are historical; delay-history features need a live feed in production.
6. **Severity model is weak** (macro-F1 0.288).
7. **Statements in the project report that this evidence does not support** (for Person 4 to correct): the abstract's "F1 score exceeding 0.70" and "substantial improvement over logistic regression"; Chapter 5's claim that SHAP confirmed `visibility_risk`, `storm_flag` and `wind_category` as leading predictors; the recommendation bands (0.50/0.80) which do not match the KPI bands used here.
